releases.name: SmedCover v0.4.0
releases.body: # SmedCover 0.4.0 This release lets AI agents make covers in SmedCover. The desktop app can serve an MCP (Model Context Protocol) endpoint on this computer, and agents such as Claude Code, Codex or Cursor connect to it and work in the window you have open. They change the words and the look, place, add and remove layers, add, crop and cut out photos, draw previews, deal hands with Surprise me, export, and make covers in a batch: 31 tools in all. You watch each change as it is made, and each one is a step of undo. Turn it on under ⋯ → *Agents*, which also gives you the line that sets your agent up. No token is needed by default, and one switch makes the endpoint require one. While the endpoint is on, the agents' lamp lights the top bar's edge. A few fixes come with it: *Reset placement* keeps a background photo filling the canvas, and a project you open no longer writes its picture over one already here. The first start's welcome can now be read in English too. ## Highlights - **Agents drive SmedCover over MCP**: the desktop app serves an endpoint at `http://127.0.0.1:25277/mcp` that listens on this computer only. An agent works in the open window through 31 tools. It reads the profiles and the cover; changes the words, the look and the layers; adds, crops, cuts out and weaves photos; draws previews; deals with Surprise me; opens projects; exports; and makes covers in a batch. - **You see what it does, and can take it back**: calls run one at a time and wait while you are in the middle of something. A change holds the window while it runs, with a pill of glass saying what is being done. Each change is one step of undo in the window's history. After 20 seconds you can *Stop waiting* (or press Esc). - **Settings → Agents**: the *MCP endpoint* switch and its port, *Require a token*, the lines to copy for Claude Code, Codex and any client that takes JSON, and the agents *Seen lately* with their calls. ⋯ → *Agents* opens it, and its line in the menu says whether the endpoint is on and on which port. - **No token by default, one switch to require one**: the endpoint takes no requests from other computers or from web pages. Turn on *Require a token* if the computer is shared, or runs containers, virtual machines or apps you do not trust. - **The agents' lamp**: while the endpoint is on, the top bar's edge is lit in the colours of dawn. *Agent access on* shows beside *Surprise me*, after a small turquoise light that breathes while an agent's change runs. ## New features and improvements ### Agents (MCP) - The endpoint is in the desktop app. It uses MCP's Streamable HTTP at `http://127.0.0.1:25277/mcp` and listens on 127.0.0.1 only, so the agent must run on this computer. Protocol revisions served: 2026-07-28, and 2025-03-26, 2025-06-18 and 2025-11-25 through `initialize`. - To turn it on, open ⋯ → *Agents* and switch on *MCP endpoint*. To use another port (1024–65535), type it under *Port* and press *Apply* or Enter. The switch is kept: while it is on, the endpoint starts with the app and stops when the app quits. - If the port cannot be had, the page says why: *Another program uses port …*, *The system reserves port …* (on Windows, ports reserved for Hyper-V, WSL or Docker), or the system's own words. The endpoint never moves to another port by itself. - One line sets up Claude Code: ```bash claude mcp add --transport http --scope user smedcover http://127.0.0.1:25277/mcp ``` *Connect an agent* also gives a table for Codex's `~/.codex/config.toml`, with `tool_timeout_sec = 1800` because Codex gives a tool only 60 seconds by default. It also gives the JSON for Claude Code's `.mcp.json` and Cursor's `mcp.json`. Every line uses the port in force. - To check that it works: in Claude Code, `/mcp` shows `smedcover` connected, with 31 tools. `curl http://127.0.0.1:25277/health` answers without a token. - What an agent reads through the endpoint (the cover, previews, photos, what it exports) goes to that agent and to the model it uses. A photo it adds by link is downloaded by SmedCover. - When an agent connects, SmedCover tells it how SmedCover works. The tools, by group: - Reading: `get_context`, `get_cover`, `list_options`, `list_library` and `render_preview` (a PNG of a cover as it will be exported, or every size on one sheet). - Text and look: `set_text`, `set_look`, `set_channel`, `set_layer_effect`, `set_layer_font`, `set_layer_bend`, `set_layer_color`. - Layers: `place_layer`, `show_layer`, `add_layer`, `remove_layer`, `reorder_layer`, and `apply_cover_json` as a last resort. - Photos: `add_photo`, `crop_photo`, `cut_out`, `weave`. - Surprise me: `surprise` (deals up to six hands and returns them on one sheet) and `pick_hand` (takes another hand). - Files and batches: `open_project`, `export`, `batch_covers`. - The window: `get_selection`, `select_layer`, `undo`, `redo`. - If the window says nothing about a call for a set time, SmedCover gives the call up. That time is 30 s for the reads, 1 minute for a change, 2 minutes for `render_preview` and `surprise`, 10 for `cut_out`, and 30 for `export` and `batch_covers`. Each word of progress starts the time again. A call given up is answered as failed, and whatever it had changed stays as one step you can undo. - When an agent cancels a call or hangs up, a call still waiting never runs. A call already running is told at once (an export stops between two files). - [README_MCP.md](https://github.com/cybertheye/smedcover/blob/v0.4.0/README_MCP.md) ([中文](https://github.com/cybertheye/smedcover/blob/v0.4.0/README_MCP.zh-CN.md)) covers it all in one place: setting up Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, and clients that speak only stdio (through `mcp-remote`); the token; how a session goes; every tool with its arguments; and a troubleshooting table. ### In the window while an agent works - Calls run one at a time, in the order they came. A call waits while you are in the middle of something: - a press or a drag, typing, or a dialog or question open - Surprise me's window, the letter, crop or weave window, or the weave brush - a file or folder being picked, or the colour picker open - a profile being made, duplicated, imported or deleted, a logo going in, or covers being exported from a table - an export you started It goes ahead once your hands have been off the window for 400 ms. After 30 seconds of waiting (10 for a read), the agent is told SmedCover is busy and tries again. - A change holds the window while it runs. After 150 ms, a pill of glass at the top says what is being done (*Changing the words*, *Exporting 3 of 12*…). A press on the window pulses the pill (*One moment — almost done*). Keys, pastes and the wheel are swallowed, not replayed later. - After 20 seconds, the pill says *Taking longer than usual* and offers *Stop waiting* (or Esc). The window is yours again, and the agent is told the step did not finish. - A change aimed at another profile or channel first switches the window there, as you would, and a toast says where (*Now on …*). Reads never switch the window. - Each change is one step of undo in the window's history. `undo` and `redo` step through that same history, yours and the agent's alike. A call that fails part-way is rolled back. - Settings can stay open while an agent works. Its page is drawn again only when a change touched what the page shows (a channel renamed, another profile shown). It keeps its scroll, and the field you were in gets back its focus, its caret and what you typed. - On macOS, the window keeps drawing while the endpoint runs, even when it is covered or on another desktop, so an agent's previews and exports do not wait for it to be seen. ### Settings → Agents - *MCP endpoint*: the switch, a pill for the state (*Off*, *Running*, *Switching…*, *Not started*), *Port* with *Apply*, and a line saying what the state means. - *Require a token*: see below. - *Connect an agent*: the lines to copy, each with its own *Copy*. A note says that a proxy in the agent's environment must leave this computer out (`NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1,localhost`). - *Seen lately*: the agents seen in the last 10 minutes (name, version, number of calls, when), the calls running and the last call (done or failed). It shows a warning when the window's tools are not those the endpoint lists. An agent stays listed for as long as one of its calls runs. Requests that cannot be tied to any agent are counted under *Unidentified agent*. - A light beside *Agents* in Settings' nav shows the endpoint's state: green while it runs, amber while it switches, red when it could not start. - In the ⋯ menu, *Agents* sits in the *Settings* group under *AI*. Its line says *Off* or *On · port 25277*. The page is in the desktop app only. - The endpoint's settings are kept in `mcp.json` in the data folder. They are not in `custom.json`, in an exported profile or in a project file. Only SmedCover writes the file, and on macOS and Linux only you can read it. A file that is not JSON is set aside as `mcp.json.bad`, and a new one is started. A file that cannot be read leaves the endpoint off, and SmedCover does not write over it. ### Require a token - It is off by default. Other computers cannot reach 127.0.0.1, and web pages are refused: a request whose `Host` or `Origin` is not this computer's gets 403, and no CORS headers are sent. SmedCover's own window cannot call the endpoint either. - While it is off, any program on this computer can use the endpoint without a token, including programs of other accounts, containers, virtual machines, WSL and sandboxed apps. Through the endpoint, such a program can: - drive the window - have SmedCover read any picture or project you can read, by naming its path - write new images into any folder you can write - have SmedCover fetch links Turn it on if the computer is shared, or runs containers, virtual machines or apps you do not trust. - While it is on, the token (`smc_` and 43 characters) is shown hidden but for its last four characters, with *Show*, *Copy* and *New token*. *New token* asks first, and the old token stops working at once. - Turning the switch on or off, or a new token, is in force from the next request, without a restart. - The lines under *Connect an agent* then carry the token, and *Copy* copies them with the token itself. - Codex's lines read the token from the `SMEDCOVER_TOKEN` environment variable, so it is not kept in `config.toml`. - Agents set up without the token get 401 and must be set up again. ### Files an agent names - `add_photo` takes one of the following, as PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, HEIC/HEIF or AVIF (told by its first bytes), 64 MB at most: - an absolute path - an http or https link, fetched through the proxy set for the image AI - a picture in the library - the picture's data itself - `open_project` takes an absolute path to a `.smedcover.json`, 128 MB at most. - SmedCover reads only pictures and projects, and reads a file only while the agent's call that names that very file is under way. - `export` and `batch_covers` never write over a file: a name already taken gets a number (`name-2.png`, `name-3.png`, …). A folder given to `export` is not kept for the profile. Your own exports from the Export window are written as before. - A request may be up to 32 MiB, so for a big photo or project the agent should give a path or a link. ### Other changes - The first start's welcome has a 中文 | English switch at the right of its title. It redraws the welcome in that language at once and keeps the brand name you typed. The starter or sample profile is made in the language chosen. - The ⋯ menu no longer ends with its note on what is kept under it. ## Fixes - *Reset placement* puts a layer back where it was put on. A photo filling the canvas still fills it; before, a background photo became a print that no longer filled the canvas. A sticker comes back at the scale it is put on at (0.3, not 0.35). - Opening a project, or importing a profile with its covers, never puts its picture in place of one already here. If the picture's id is taken by another picture, it comes in under an id of its own. Before, a project could write its picture over one that other covers showed, and undo could not bring it back. - A change to a profile is saved to that profile even when another profile is shown before the save is written. Before, a change of look followed at once by a switch of profile could be lost at the next start. - If the app cannot open or make its data folder, a dialog now says so in Chinese and English before the app quits. Before, the window flashed up and vanished without a word. - In Settings, the page's title and the line under it stay still above the scrolling page, so a card's border no longer runs under the ✕ when a long page is scrolled. ## Upgrading from 0.3.1 - The agents' endpoint is off until you turn it on. Until then, nothing listens. - On first start, the app makes `mcp.json` in the data folder: the endpoint off, port 25277, and a new token, not required. - When SmedCover is updated, restart your agent too (or reconnect it from its MCP menu) so that it reads the new list of tools. ## Installing | System | File | |---|---| | macOS (Intel) | `SmedCover_0.4.0_x64.dmg`, and `.app.tar.gz` | | macOS (Apple silicon) | `SmedCover_0.4.0_aarch64.dmg`, and `.app.tar.gz` | | Windows x64 | `.exe`, `.msi` | | Linux x64 | `.deb`, `.rpm`, `.AppImage` | - On a Mac, open the `.dmg` and drag SmedCover into Applications. - The installers are built by GitHub Actions. - On Windows and Linux, cutting out a subject uses the BiRefNet model, downloaded once under *Settings → AI → Cut-out*. Until it is downloaded, an agent's `cut_out` answers `unavailable`. ## Known issues - The endpoint has not been tried with Hermes Agent or OpenClaw yet. A few tool arguments take one of two forms (`"all"` or a list; a channel's name or its number). Whether every model takes them as they are is still to be checked (Gemini's stricter JSON Schema, for one). - The agent must run on this computer. An agent on another machine cannot reach the endpoint. An agent in a Docker Desktop container usually gets 403, because it addresses the computer as `host.docker.internal`. On Linux, a container on Docker Engine's bridge network cannot reach the endpoint at all; one with `--network host` can. - Only on macOS does the window keep drawing while it is hidden. Windows slows a minimised window down, so previews and exports stall while it is minimised there: keep it on screen while an agent works. - A client of the older protocol revisions cancels a call with a separate notification. SmedCover acts on it only when it can tie it to exactly one call; otherwise the call runs to its end. Hanging up always cancels. - Agents cannot yet make or delete profiles, add or remove channels, change the profile's sizes, import fonts, use AI generation, photo repaint or AI stickers, or change settings (the endpoint's own among them). - The window has not been tried on real Windows (WebView2) or Linux (WebKitGTK) machines. The window buttons drawn there were checked only in a browser. On Windows 10 there may be a 1 px light line along the top, and on Windows 11 hovering over maximise no longer shows the snap layouts. - While the app is in the background, the first click on the top bar only brings the window to the front. - On a Mac, *Saved as you go* is not shown in the top bar while the window is under 1200 px wide. - In a very short window, Surprise me's content can scroll under the strip along the top, where a press moves the window. - Exporting from the Export window to the remembered folder replaces a file of the same name without asking, as before. - The cover standards use estimated feed widths and badge positions for each platform. They have not yet been measured from real phone screenshots. - While a slider is dragged, the canvas shows a draft and finishes when you let go. For Risograph's *overprinted shapes*, Cyberpunk's *colour split* and a few Glitch net art and Dark deco sliders, the draft differs visibly from the finished picture.

releases.name: SmedCover v0.3.1
releases.body: # SmedCover 0.3.1 This release redraws the whole window in frosted glass. The cover, blurred, is the ground, and every panel is a pane over it. A top bar holds the profile and channel, undo, Surprise me and Export. A dock of five sheets (Content, Look, Layout, Assets, Layers) takes the place of the Cover, Style and Assets tabs, and the selected layer has a bar of its most used settings right over it on the canvas. Looks, text effects and layout presets are cards drawn with your cover: hover over one to preview it on the canvas. Surprise me, Export, AI repaint and AI generate are windows of their own. The app also starts faster, and the slowest look effects are many times faster. ## Highlights - **A frosted-glass window**: a top bar (profile and channel, undo and redo, Surprise me, Export and a ⋯ menu), a dock of five sheets, a tray under the canvas with the sizes and *Applies to*, and the selected layer's properties in a drawer on the right, shut until you need it. Setup is now a Settings window over the editor. The window has no system title bar: its buttons sit at the top bar's left end, and dragging the top bar moves the window. You can turn the glass off under ⋯ to get plain panels. - **A bar over the selected layer**: a lettering layer's font, colours, effect, bend and columns; a photo's background, crop, AI repaint and replacement; an asset's colour, crop and weave; a colour layer's colour. Each opens its controls in a popover you can drag aside. *More…* opens the drawer. - **Cards you can preview**: every look, every text effect and every layout preset is a card drawn with your own cover. Hover over a card for a moment to see it on the canvas; click it to use it. Looks can be searched, filtered by kind (Night, Illustration, Poster, Print, Experimental), shown by ★ Most used, and liked into ♥ Liked. - **Surprise me takes the whole window**: the six hands are as large as they fit, each naming its look, ground, lettering and layout. Lock Look, Ground, Lettering, Places or (new) Layout. Space deals, and deals again in the window. Esc or *Undo the deal* puts the cover back. The chances are cards with dots: each dot makes a look twice as likely. - **Export made over**: each size with its picture, ticks for the sizes to export (All, Wide only, Tall only), file names as chips, and exports go to the last folder without asking (kept for each profile). ⌘E (Ctrl+E) opens it. - **Faster**: from the second launch on, the Look sheet opens with every card already drawn. The first frame comes sooner. A cover whose photo uses Record sleeve's halftone shows in under a second instead of over five. Outline-style look effects are up to 13× faster. ## New features and improvements ### The window - Frosted glass: the cover, small and blurred, is the window's ground, and fades into a new cover over 0.7 s. Where the web view cannot blur, or with *Frosted glass* turned off under ⋯, the panes are plain. - If dragging is slow with the glass on, a note says so once on this computer when you let go, with a button that makes the panels plain. The glass only changes when you change it. - No system title bar on macOS, Windows or Linux. The close, minimise and zoom buttons are at the top bar's left end. The top bar and the window's margin move the window, and a double click there zooms it. While Settings, a dialog or Surprise me covers the top bar, a strip along the top still moves the window. - A narrow window keeps the canvas in view: the one-under-another arrangement is now only for windows 1000 px wide and under (the desktop app's window is at least 1080). Where the sheet, the drawer and the canvas don't all fit, the drawer takes the sheet's place. - The ⋯ menu shows how many channels and sizes the profile has, switches profiles, opens Settings, and has a *Project file* group: *Open project…* (⌘O / Ctrl+O) and *Save project* (⌘S / Ctrl+S). - The profile and channel lists in the top bar end in *+ New…*. - What cannot be undone asks first, in a window of the app's own. - The properties drawer and every other window use the same controls: scrub bars, switches, segments and lists. Each group is a line that says what it is set to while shut and opens to its controls. Groups are in the order they are most often changed, and buttons show an icon before their name. ### Content, Layout and Assets - Content holds the channel and the cover's words. Longer notes are behind an ⓘ. - Layout presets are cards in the Layout sheet, each with a picture of this cover laid out by it: rename, apply, edit, delete, or *+ New*. Hover over a card to see the layout on the canvas. - With the Layout sheet open, every layout part on the canvas (title, subtitle, tag, brand row, channel name and graphic, logo, colour block) is framed in a dashed line with its name. - The colour block has *Size & slant* in its properties: Band, Side panel or Slim banner, with Mirror. *Block by orientation* lays every size out by its orientation in one go. - New default layouts for each orientation: wide sizes with a side panel on the right, tall sizes stacked with a band at the bottom, square sizes with a banner. New profiles, sizes added later, new layout presets and *Restore this template's defaults* start from them. Profiles you already have stay as they were. - *Applies to* starts at the canvas's orientation (All wide, All square or All tall) every time the app starts. - The layout preset editor: buttons for each side the colour block may lie on (Bottom, Top, Right, Left), *Reset size and slant* and *Reset its place* as two buttons, a Vertical switch for the title, subtitle, tag and channel name, the brand logo as a part, and up to eight elements of your own. The parts list and the selected part's settings scroll on their own. - The Assets sheet can be searched (photos, stickers, channel graphics, your vector assets), and the photo shelf can be filtered by kind. - Photos come in as prints above the selected layer, the first one too. *Fill the canvas* takes a photo down to the ground, just above the Background. - A channel name that doesn't sit on the colour block is lettered in the channel colour with its outline, so it reads over the photo. ### Layers - Each row shows a tile of what the layer holds, its name, a grey line saying what it holds or that it isn't shown at this size, and a chip for the sizes it is kept to. Its eye and lock show under the pointer, and the row under the pointer is framed on the canvas. Rows that can be dragged have a ⋮⋮ grip. - Chips over the list narrow it to All, Mine (the layers you added) or Layout (the layout's own), with a Focus button (F). - Dragging a layout part in the list also makes that order the profile's default. - The Background row stays at the foot of the list, and the 3D view opens at once however many layers there are. ### Looks and lettering - The Look sheet: a card for every look, drawn with your cover. Search by name in either language, by what a look says of itself or by its kinds. Filter by kind, ★ Most used (the looks this computer has put on most often) and ♥ Liked (click the heart on a card). The sheet scrolls to the look in use. - Text effects are cards in the Effect group and the bar's popover: each shows the layer's first letter in that effect, in its own face and colours. *Automatic* comes first, then the layer's own, then the rest, with *See all* for every effect. - A lettering layer's bar: its font, its colours as one round button (the words' and the highlighted words' colours), Effect, Bend, Vertical, and More…. ### Surprise me - A window over the whole app with the cover dimmed behind it. The hands are laid out in two, three or six columns by the size's shape, and the one on the canvas is marked. - Under the hands: the parts to leave alone, the chances, *Deal again* and *Done*. - *Layout* can be locked: every hand keeps the canvas's layout and no layout preset is dealt. - Space deals from the editor, and deals again in the window. It never deals while a deal is under way, and never while you are typing. - The chances are cards: each look has its picture, its share and a row of dots, every look on three to begin with. Your chances are kept as they were. ### Export - The Export window shows each size with its picture, name and pixels. Tick the sizes to export (*All*, *Wide only*, *Tall only*; square sizes go with tall), or export one size alone from its row. - *Save to* shows the folder and *Change*. Exports go there without asking again, and the folder is kept for each profile. - The file name pattern is shown as chips (Number, Channel, Code, Title, Size, Width, Height) with the text between them typed in place. - Batch export from a table has moved to *Settings → Sizes & export*. ### AI - *AI repaint* is a window: the original beside the result, with *Discard*, *Try again*, *Use this* and the way back to the original. What to paint it as sits beside them: the current look, the built-in styles as chips, and your own styles with their editor. - *AI generate* is a window: *Photo* or *Stickers & graphics*, the kinds as cards, a reference picture dragged in or picked, and the service and model. *Made this session* keeps up to twelve results as thumbnails, to look at again, add or save. - Each AI service has a light: grey when not set up, green when ready, amber while working, red when the last request failed. The ⋯ menu shows all three as one. ### Settings - Settings has the profile and its actions (new, duplicate, import, export, delete) in its nav. *Brand & channels* shows the channels as cards; drag one by its ⋮⋮ grip to reorder. *Sizes & export* has a row per size. *AI* is three cards on one page (text, image, cut-out). - The app's defaults are in one file, `ui/defaults.json`. The settings you choose are kept in `custom.json` in the data folder, and only what differs from the defaults is written there. A `custom.json` you edit by hand is laid over the defaults key by key; a name the app doesn't know, or a value of the wrong kind, is left out, and you are told once. ### Performance Measured in the Mac app (release build): - **The Look sheet's cards are kept from one launch to the next** (`lookcards/` in the data folder). On the second launch the sheet opens full and redraws only cards whose cover changed: the visible cards took 3.2 s and all of them 7.8 s; now both are there at once. - **Glyph outlines are kept from one launch to the next** (`outlines.json`, up to 8 MB), so lettering reshaped by an effect draws at once on the canvas, the look cards and the 3D view. - **Startup** reads the system fonts, imported fonts, profiles, covers and assets side by side, and the ransom note finds its faces only when it is first drawn (about 340 ms saved). Page load to first frame: 1.22–1.44 s → 0.87–0.92 s. - **Halftone and stipple**: Record sleeve's photo halftone and Spectral engraving's Stipple work out their dots pixel by pixel instead of filling tens of thousands of circles. For a cover with the halftone on its background photo: first frame 5.2–6.3 s → 0.83 s, 3D view 16–21 s → 1.5 s, all look cards 66–79 s → 5.2 s. - **Look effects that stack many copies of a layer** do it on the graphics card. Measured on a layer filling the canvas at the editor's width: two-tone outline 1.41 s → 0.11 s, varsity outline 0.77 → 0.08, sunlit block 0.74 → 0.10, paper lift 0.60 → 0.09, comic colouring 0.43 → 0.17, motion blur 0.38 → 0.03, Silent wasteland's strokes 0.88 → 0.70. - **The 3D view** repaints only the sheets that changed: with 21 layers, its first frame went from about 1.35 s to about 40 ms. - The layout preset cards are drawn one at a time while the app is idle, so the Layout sheet no longer slows editing. ## Fixes - Picking a look no longer makes the canvas shrink and the size bar jump for a moment. - The sheets, the drawer, Settings and the look cards no longer shift when a scrollbar appears or goes. - An open group's chevron no longer takes the click meant for its line. - A value typed into a bar no longer swallows a click on a button elsewhere: *Done* in the chances shuts the window, and *Lock* in the letter window locks the letter. - In *Settings → AI*, the Anthropic authentication choice no longer covers the reply-length bar. - A selected chip or button keeps its look under the pointer. - On a Mac, a press inside the editor no longer ends a name you are typing. - Self-test from source: it finds the installed fonts it needs by trying them one at a time, not all 1,600 of a well-stocked Mac (its first start no longer waits 53 s). It also times every look effect and fails on one that would take over 4 s. ## Upgrading from 0.2.0 - This is the first release since 0.2.0. 0.3.0 was tagged, but its build failed on Windows and it was never released. - On first start your settings are carried over from `settings.json` to `custom.json` in the same data folder. `settings.json` is left as it was and is no longer written. A `custom.json` that is not valid JSON is kept as `custom.json.bad` rather than written over. - Profiles and covers open as they are, and your layouts stay as they were. The new default layouts apply only where a layout starts afresh. - The properties drawer starts shut: double-click the canvas, or use *More…* on the bar over the selected layer. - The batch export from a table is under *Settings → Sizes & export*. - `lookcards/` and `outlines.json` in the data folder are caches and can be deleted; the app draws them again. ## Installing | System | File | |---|---| | macOS (Intel) | `SmedCover_0.3.1_x64.dmg`, and `.app.tar.gz` | | macOS (Apple silicon) | `SmedCover_0.3.1_aarch64.dmg`, and `.app.tar.gz` | | Windows x64 | `.exe`, `.msi` | | Linux x64 | `.deb`, `.rpm`, `.AppImage` | - On a Mac, open the `.dmg` and drag SmedCover into Applications. - The installers are built by GitHub Actions. - On Windows and Linux, cutting out a subject uses the BiRefNet model, downloaded once under *Settings → AI → Cut-out*. ## Known issues - The new window has not been tried on real Windows (WebView2) or Linux (WebKitGTK) machines. The window buttons drawn there were checked only in a browser: on Windows 10 there may be a 1 px light line along the top, and on Windows 11 hovering over maximise no longer shows the snap layouts. - While the app is in the background, the first click on the top bar only brings the window to the front. - On a Mac, *Saved as you go* is not shown in the top bar while the window is under 1200 px wide. - In a very short window, Surprise me's content can scroll under the strip along the top, where a press moves the window. - Exporting to the remembered folder replaces a file of the same name without asking, as before. - The cover standards use estimated feed widths and badge positions for each platform; they have not yet been measured from real phone screenshots. - While a slider is dragged the canvas shows a draft and finishes when you let go. For Risograph's *overprinted shapes*, Cyberpunk's *colour split* and a few Glitch net art and Dark deco sliders, the draft differs visibly from the finished picture.

releases.name: SmedCover v0.2.0
releases.body: # SmedCover 0.2.0 This release adds five looks (35 in all), lets each output size have a layout of its own and each layer show at only some sizes, and turns Surprise me into a deal of six hands, with chances you can set and layout presets it can deal. Lettering gains a subtitle, vertical setting, bends that work with any lettering and several new text effects. Cut-outs and assets can weave with the words, photos and assets can be cropped to any shape, and dragging a look's sliders is much smoother. ## Highlights - **Five new looks**: City pop night, Constructivist, Dark deco, Silent wasteland and Origami noir. Each has its own sliders, scene objects to drag and look effects, and paints a photo its own way: Origami noir cuts it into triangular facets, Silent wasteland paints it over in brush strokes. - **A layout for each size**: 16:9 can be side by side while 3:4 is stacked. *Applies to* has a new middle choice, *All wide / All square / All tall*, and *Wide side by side, tall and square stacked* sets every size in one click. *Shown at* keeps a layer to some sizes only (no subtitle on 9:16, say), and its room goes to the title. - **Layout presets**: save where the title, subtitle, tag, channel name, brand row, channel graphic and colour block stand at every size, and lay them out in a layout editor of their own. Apply one to the canvas, or let Surprise me deal it. - **Surprise me deals six hands**: each in a different look, shown in a window as they are dealt. Click one to put it on the canvas (still one step of undo). Lock the look, ground, lettering or places, and set how likely every choice is in Surprise me's chances. - **Weave**: a cut-out subject, or a sticker, graphic, uploaded image or 3D object, can pass in front of and behind the lettering below it, the way a head covers a magazine's masthead. Split it at the head automatically, choose letter by letter, or paint it with a brush. - **Crop**: photos and assets have *Crop…*: any ratio, their own shape, the usual ratios, or *Free* for a shape of any outline. Nothing is lost; *No crop* brings back the whole picture. - **Vertical**: every lettering layer can be set in columns, right to left, as in a Song-dynasty printed book, with *Column rules* if you like. Text effects, outline and shadow, plates and highlight styles all work in columns. - **More lettering**: a subtitle under the title. *Bend* is its own setting now, works with any lettering, has 8 new bends and 8 handles to reshape it by hand. New text effects: Sticker, six outlined effects (spiky, torn edge, scissor-cut, melting, puffed up, eaten away) and the ransom note. Highlighted words can be ringed, marked or set on an offset block. ## New features and improvements ### Looks - Five new looks, from 30 to 35: - **City pop night**: the city by night on late-80s anime videotapes, with cel-painted clouds and towers, neon signs and lights doubled in the water. The channel graphic becomes a cel figure with a neon rim; a photo is painted in four flat cel tones. - **Constructivist**: the Soviet avant-garde poster. The channel graphic is rebuilt as a machine of grey, ink, paper and red rectangles, with wedges, a disc, rays and a steel truss; the red can turn to the channel colour by degrees. - **Dark deco**: Gotham's Art Deco night as the 90s animated series painted it. The title is lit like a theatre front's lamps, highlighted words are neon in the channel colour, and a photo is painted into the ultramarine night. - **Silent wasteland**: the quiet world after the end as concept painters paint it, in broad brush and palette-knife strokes under one low sun. A photo is painted over stroke by stroke. - **Origami noir**: a rain-soaked neo-noir night as faceted, low-poly flat illustration, with giant neon letters in the mist. A photo is cut into triangular facets that keep a face's eyes and mouth. - *Figure from*: the 21 looks that draw a figure from the channel graphic can draw it from another graphic, one of your assets, a sticker, an uploaded picture or a photo's cut-out subject (cut out on this computer). - The Background has a base: *Grid* (the look's ground with a grid drawn the look's way; the default), *Look's own* (the ground as the look first had it, no grid) or *See-through*. Every look's scene is painted on the base; with all its sliders at nothing, only the base is left. - Woodblock book's *Set the title vertically* now sets the subtitle in columns too. - Jelly machine has a new *board size* slider. ### Layout and sizes - Each size can have its own layout (template and adjustments). The other sizes follow the profile's default. A size with its own layout says *This size has its own layout*, offers *Follow again*, and has a small diamond on its thumbnail. - *Applies to* gains *Same orientation* (the button reads *All wide*, *All square* or *All tall*): one change reaches every size facing the same way, a move scaled to each canvas. - *Wide side by side, tall and square stacked* gives every size a fitting layout in one click, as one step of undo. - *Shown at*: every layer but the background can be shown at some sizes only. At the other sizes it is as if left out: not in the export, the thumbnail or the 3D view, and a layout layer's room goes to the rest. The layer list labels it (*Only 3:4*, *Only tall*, *Not 9:16*). - With *Applies to* on one size or one orientation, *Cut out subject* and *Remove the background* act at those sizes only. - *Cover → Layout parts*: a row for each part the layout brings. Untick one to leave it out of this cover; drag rows to re-order the layers, which also becomes the profile's default order. - Layout presets: up to 24, for every profile, kept on this computer. Create, edit, apply or delete them in Surprise me's chances. In the layout editor, drag the colour block's diamonds to size and slant it, drag the block to another side, and add sizes of the preset's own. - The layouts keep to the cover standards: on 16:9 and 4:3 no words and no graphic sit under the apps' duration and play-count badges; on other sizes words keep out of the bottom 14%; the title's box holds two lines at 14 px in the narrowest feed; in *Stack* the channel graphic takes at least 12% of the cover; a part left out gives its room to the others. - A new cover comes with the tag `EP.01` and a placeholder subtitle, and leaves out the channel name and channel graphic, so the title is larger. Tick them under *Layout parts* to bring them back. - Preset sizes are named after the platforms, one per ratio: *Bilibili / YouTube · 16:9*, *Bilibili / Douyin / WeChat Channels · 4:3*, *Douyin / RED / WeChat Channels · 3:4*, *YouTube · 9:16*, *WeChat article · 1:1*, *WeChat article · 2.35:1*, all on for a new profile. Thumbnails under the canvas show the ratio; hover for the name and pixels. ### Lettering - Subtitle: a smaller line under the title, lettered as the title is; the title makes room for it. Type it under *Subtitle*, or untick it under *Layout parts*. - *Vertical* and *Column rules* on the title, subtitle, text layers, corner tag, channel name, brand row and copies of them. - Titles are set as a typesetter would set Chinese: Latin letters and digits beside Chinese are set as tall as the characters, and Chinese punctuation is squeezed in the Kaiming style, so titles come out a little larger. - *Bend* is its own setting and bends any lettering: the look's own, every text effect, plates and highlight marks, and look effects. New bends: arc down, on a circle, arched top, bulge, pinch, fisheye, rise and flag, 11 in all with arched, tapered and wave. Every bend but Tapered has four diamond handles along the top and four along the bottom to reshape it; *Reset the shape* undoes that. - New text effects: - *Sticker*: the letters run together on a thick white rim, as in variety-show captions. - Outlined: *spiky*, *torn edge*, *scissor-cut*, *melting*, *puffed up* and *eaten away* reshape the letters' own outlines (desktop app only). All but puffed up have *Reshuffle*. - *Ransom note*: each letter as if cut from another paper; some stand in depth, are cut from the photo, sit on torn scraps or are taped down. *Letter by letter…* dresses or locks them one at a time. - *Extruded* is now listed with the layered letterings. - *Highlight style* for words in `*asterisks*`: colour only, plates, a ring drawn round, a marker, or an offset block, in a colour of its own. - The title can do what a text layer does: take look effects, *Clip to the layer below*, and have its words edited in its properties. ### Layers and editing - *3D*: the first button above the layer list takes the cover apart into a stack of sheets seen at an angle, so you can see what each layer holds and what lies over what. Turn it, spread the sheets, click one to select its layer. - *FOCUS* now dims the other layers on the canvas, greys them in the list and keeps them from being selected. - Layout layers can be copied (Cmd/Ctrl + D; all but Background and Corner brackets). The copy shows what the layout's own does, in a style and place of its own, and can be deleted and renamed. - *Crop…* on photos and every asset opens a window over the left column, with the canvas still in view: *Any ratio*, *Its own shape*, 1:1, 4:3, 3:4, 16:9, 9:16, or *Free*, where you add and remove points for any outline. The outline, torn edge and shadow follow the cropped shape. - *Weave* on cut-outs and assets, three ways: *Automatic (head in front)* (*Automatic (top in front)* on an asset), *Letter by letter* and *Brush*. Strokes are kept in the photo's or asset's own proportions, so they follow it when it is moved or scaled, and at every size. - A photo's outline can be *Dashed*, like the line a sticker is cut along. ### Surprise me - Deals six hands at a time, each in a different look, shown in a window over the left column as they come. The first goes on the canvas; click another to put it there instead, still one step of undo. - Choose what the next deal leaves alone: the *Look* (with its sliders), the *Ground*, the *Lettering* or the *Places*. - Surprise me's chances: set how likely each look, colour block shape, title lettering, bend and ground is, how many look effects other layers get and from which look, plus switches and each look's optional parts. Layout presets have a chance there too. - Each look is dealt by its own recipe: mostly its own lettering, sliders near its defaults, parts that are off by default only now and then (two at most). *How Surprise me deals this look* in the Style tab changes those chances. - It reads the cover: a long title is bent less and less often given a sticker's rim or depth; the ground keeps away from one the channel colour would sink into; your layers are placed clear of the title and cut-out subjects where they can be, and your text above the bottom 14%. - After a deal the title is on top (but for a cut-out that already stood over it), words you moved or resized go back where the rules put them, and woven layers and their lettering stay where they are. ### AI - The five new looks each have their own description for *AI repaint* with *Follow the current look*, and their own style for AI-generated vector assets. ### Export - With the Background's base on *See-through*, PNG and WebP export with a transparent background (JPEG is still filled dark). - Batch export: the CSV takes a fourth column for the subtitle, each row using only its own. - A layer kept to some sizes appears only in those sizes' exports. - The export dialog names sizes after the platforms. ### Performance - Dragging a look's slider repaints only the layers that use it, draws a photo's blurred, grey and tinted copies from the graphics card, and paints the canvas once a frame and one thumbnail a frame. Measured in the Mac app with a 4000 × 3000 photo filling the canvas: Monochrome film went from 3-9 to 58-62 frames a second, Dark deco from 3-8 to 36-45, Avant-garde image from 16-18 to 54-60. - Silent wasteland and Origami noir keep a bounded cache of what they paint and release all of it when you switch to another look. ### Other - *Brand logo*: upload a logo under *Setup → Brand*. It stands at the right end of the brand row on every channel's cover as the *Brand logo* layer, to move, resize or hide. Looks that print in that corner move aside. - *Show the number in the brand row*: the "SERIES 01 / 05" counter is now optional, and off by default. - Upgrading from 0.1.0: - Covers open with the Background's base on *Grid*, so looks with a ground of their own show grid lines. Choose *Look's own* for how they looked before. - Covers never touched (still on the placeholder title) get the tag `EP.01` and a placeholder subtitle once, and leave out the channel name and graphic. Tick them to bring them back. - A title or text that used Arched, Tapered or Wave as its text effect opens as *Outline and shadow* with the same bend, looking as before. - Self-test from source: `SMEDCOVER_SELFTEST_LOOKS` limits it to some looks. ## Fixes - The dashed FOCUS frame no longer flickers on the canvas while FOCUS is off. - Lettering in a font you installed, or one macOS downloads on demand (Kaiti, Xingkai, Weibei and others), no longer falls back to the default font once a look effect is applied. - Jelly machine: moving the *jelly figure* slider no longer resizes the board and lays its circuit out again. - Windows: an AI request that waits too long shows the app's own timeout message (raise the timeout under *Setup → AI*, or use a faster model) instead of the system's "os error 10060". - Windows: text files keep LF line endings on checkout, so `npm test` passes there too (affects building from source). - The self-test no longer stalls when its window opens off screen. ## Installing | System | File | |---|---| | macOS (Intel) | `SmedCover_0.2.0_x64.dmg`, and `.app.tar.gz` | | macOS (Apple silicon) | `.dmg`, `.app.tar.gz` | | Windows x64 | `.exe`, `.msi` | | Linux x64 | `.deb`, `.rpm`, `.AppImage` | - On a Mac, open the `.dmg` and drag SmedCover into Applications. - The installers are built by GitHub Actions. The Windows and Linux builds are new in this release and less tested: they have not been tried on real machines yet. - On Windows and Linux, cutting out a subject uses the BiRefNet model, downloaded once under *Setup → AI → Cut-out*. - Profiles and covers live in the system's app data folder; the new version reads them as they are (see *Upgrading from 0.1.0* above for what changes). ## Known issues - The Windows and Linux builds have not been tried on real machines yet. - The cover standards use estimated feed widths and badge positions for each platform; they have not yet been measured from real phone screenshots. - While a slider is dragged the canvas shows a draft and finishes when you let go. For Risograph's *overprinted shapes*, Cyberpunk's *colour split* and a few Glitch net art and Dark deco sliders, the draft differs visibly from the finished picture. - With the channel graphic shown, the *Split* template's title column is narrow at portrait sizes: a line of more than 5 characters is set smaller than the feeds read well.
